The *Kadambapupphiyattheraapadāna* is a short verse narrative belonging to the Therāpadāna collection within the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Like other biographical poems in this genre, it recounts the past karmic deed of an elder—associated here with the offering of a *kadamba* flower—and the subsequent spiritual and heavenly fruits that culminated in his liberation [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral notes five modern translations across five languages for this text [SuttaCentral].

No curated parallels or significant cross-language alignments with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections are reported by SuttaCentral or DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. The closest textual alignment occurs with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (first part, segments 0.3–5.3 matching commentary section 2652_11–2661, alongside further matches in the second part) [DharmaNexus].
